summary: Long pulse shadowing: sustained long-lived streams causing KV cache growth and transient GPU credit drain in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customers in a subset of dedicated pools observed sustained P99 and P50 throughput regression beginning 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC. Root trigger: a tenant running many long-lived low-CPU, high-GPU attention streams (chat sessions) produced persistent KV cache growth which pushed allocator heartbeats and evicted small-stream slots. The allocator and autoscaler reacted by delaying new GPU attaches, which amplified queueing for other tenants in the same reserved cluster.

Impact:
- NebulaApps (dedicated) experienced 30-45% reduction in effective throughput for batched routes and a p99 latency spike from ~120ms to ~1.2s for ~40 minutes.
- Automatic fallback routed some requests to lower-capacity variants causing increased cost and degraded outputs for a brief window.
- No data loss; requests were delayed but eventually completed.

Environment:
- prod us-west-2 dedicated cluster pool-az3-resv-09
- Affected model variants: redwood/gptx-14b-quant (multi-tenant) and redwood/opt-6.7b-int8 pinned by customer routes

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. Recreate long-lived client streams with many simultaneous keepalive connections that emit sparse token output (simulate 1k concurrent sessions, 1 token/15s).
2. Configure the tenant's route to pin gptx-14b-quant with batch-size=32 and keepalive windows enabled.
3. Observe KV cache growth on serving nodes (kv-cache size monotonic increase) and allocator attach delays.
4. Measure throughput and p99 latency across co-located tenants.

Observed artifacts and logs:
- Serving runtime logs show repeated KV cache pin warnings: "kv_cache: growth=+1.2GB/min, eviction-latency=120ms"
- Allocator metrics: "slot_attach_delay" increased from ~30ms to 800ms during peak.
- Autoscaler telemetry: delayed scale-up due to aggregated attach failures and a conservative cooldown window.
- Console trace: sudden rise in per-route queue depth for NebulaApps routes between 09:22-09:58 UTC.

Initial mitigation applied:
- 09:40 UTC: Temporarily enforced per-tenant connection throttle on NebulaApps to limit long-lived sessions to their committed concurrency.
- 09:45 UTC: Evicted stale KV cache entries on a subset of serving nodes after coordination with runtime team, reducing memory pressure.
- 09:50 UTC: Increased autoscaler aggressiveness for the affected reserved pool (shorten cooldown and increase attach retry attempts) to bring attach latency back to normal.

Notes on customer communication:
- Customer reported through support channel at 09:30 UTC and was updated at 09:42 UTC with the temporary throttle plan. Customer accepted the throttle and confirmed improved p50 after throttle enforcement.

Next steps documented here and follow-up tasks captured in investigation notes below.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Noisy tenant with long-lived sessions causing KV cache growth and eviction pressure (primary).
- NVLink or PCIe contention causing attach latencies (ruled out by host-level telemetry).
- Autoscaler misclassification due to heartbeat silence from overloaded allocators (contributing factor).

Findings:
- KV cache metrics correlated tightly with slot_attach_delay and allocator evictions. One tenant's session footprint grew >1TB aggregate across the pool, causing eviction thrash.
- Autoscaler cooldown (120s) plus conservative attach retry logic meant cluster did not immediately scale for transient attach failures.
- Scheduler heartbeat lag increased by 40-60ms which pushed small-stream slots into eviction path.

Relevant links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/allocator/kv-growth?orgId=1&from=2026-03-10T09:00:00Z&to=2026-03-10T11:00:00Z
- Logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/nebulaapps/2026-03-10/attach-failures
- Slack thread: #incidents - https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/INC12345

Temporary mitigations tried and outcome:
- Per-tenant connection throttle: immediate p50 improvement, reduced KV growth rate by ~70% in 15m.
- Targeted KV prune: reclaimed ~2.1GB/node; reduced eviction latencies.
- Autoscaler tweak: improved attach recovery but needs a longer-term change to avoid oscillation.
resolution:
Short-term (applied):
- Enforced tenant-level connection limits for NebulaApps until policy hardening is complete.
- Forced KV prune and node restart sequencing to avoid simultaneous eviction spikes.
- Tuned autoscaler cooldown and retry thresholds for the affected reserved pool (deployed to prod 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC).

Long-term (in progress / backlog):
- Implement per-tenant KV quotas and auto-trim policy to prevent a single tenant from growing KV state unbounded.
- Add a KV-growth signal to autoscaler as an input (RFC opened and linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/402).
- Improve console alerts to detect long-pulse shadowing patterns earlier (runbook update scheduled).

Customer follow-up and closure notes:
- NebulaApps accepted the temporary throttle and requested a post-incident writeup. Postmortem draft created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/Incident+2026-03-LongPulse+Postmortem.
- Ticket closed after 48h stable metrics and customer confirmation.

Follow-up owner: Marco Rivera (SRE). Backlog epic: INT-900112 (KV quotas and autoscaler signal).
